To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the magnetic anisotropies of MBE-grown rare-earth iron compounds are not the bulk values.
the first-order term is not the only term that involves the shear strain ε xy in MBE-grown [110] REFe2 films.

the magnetic anisotropies in MBE-grown [110]-oriented films of rare-earth-iron compounds are not the usual bulk values, but are instead modified by the shear strain εyx frozen in during crystal growth.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the magnetic properties of REFe2 films grown by molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) on GaAs(100) substrates.
the magnetic anisotropies in MBE-grown rare earth iron compounds, which are of interest for applications in magnetic recording and magneto-optic devices.
the effects of shear strain on magnetic anisotropies in [110] REFe2 films.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the magnetic anisotropies of MBE-grown [110] REFe2 films differ from those of the bulk in that the first-order term is reduced by a few percent, while the second-order terms are enhanced by a factor of ∼3.

the magnetic anisotropies of MBE-grown [110] REFe2 films are more complicated than those of bulk REFe2, and the magnetic anisotropic properties of MBE-growth films are not simply a function of the bulk anisotropy and the shear strain.
the first-order magnetic anisotropies in [110]-grown REFe2 films are larger than those in the bulk by ∼10%, while the second-order terms are smaller by ∼15% to ∼20%.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the magnetic anisotropies in [110] REFe2 films are dominated by the shear strain εy, and that the shear strain εx, the cubic crystal field term B2 and the uniaxial crystal field term B0 are of minor importance.
the first-order term is the dominant term, but the rank-two and rank-four terms should be added in.

, for MBE-grown [110] REFe2 films (RE, Tb, Dy, Ho, Er, and Tm), the first-order term is the dominant contribution to the magnetic anisotropies, but the presence of the shear strain εy x leads to a significant increase in the magnitude of the first-order term, and the presence of several other terms, some of which are important.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the magnetic anisotropies in MBE-grown [110] REFe2 films can be quite different from those in the bulk, and the differences are due to the presence and magnitude of the shear strain εy.
the magnetic anisotropies of REFe2 films grown along the [110] axis, and hence their magnetoelastic properties, are significantly different from those in the bulk.
the magnetic anisotropies for REFe2 films in the [110] direction are more complicated than previously believed.
